To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the best use of inherent features can lead to an increase in accuracy of between 20% to 50%, that tweet content and the user’s self reported location, as well as his or her real name, are the best inherent features for country-level location classification, and that it is possible to leverage a model trained on a historical dataset to classify tweets in a real-time manner.
(a) tweet content and metadata are complementary and can be used together to accurately classify tweets in a real-time manner, and (b) a model trained on past tweets is useful to classify new ones.

(1) tweet-inherent features can be used to classify tweets at country-level in a real-time manner, (2) a model trained on one year of historical tweets can still achieve comparable performance on a year’s worth of new tweets and (3) the choice of features to use is critical, and a combination of tweet content and metadata, as opposed to tweet content alone, can lead to a significant improvement in performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a real-world, real-time scenario, which is a challenge that has not been addressed in previous work.
the classification of tweets at the country-level in a real-time, global context.
a real-time, country-level classification of worldwide tweets, and it provides some useful insights into the use of different tweet-inherent features.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best use of a particular feature depends on the country and the language in which it is written.
the choice of the right combination of features, as well as their use in a real-time setting, are crucial to achieving high accuracy in country-level classification of global tweets.

, for a given country, the best choice of features for classification depends on its characteristics, such as the language spoken, its geographical location and the number of commonalities with other countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a model trained on a large amount of historical tweets can still achieve a high level of performance when classifying new tweets, provided that the features used are not too sensitive to time.
a combination of tweet content and metadata, such as the user’s selfreported location and real name, are particularly effective for country-level classification of worldwide tweets.

a model trained from a year-old data can achieve a classification accuracy comparable to that of a model trained from the most recent data, provided that the model is built from a suitable combination of tweet-inherent, real-time features.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a country-level classification of global tweets is possible in a real-time setting, with the use of a combination of features, such as the user’s real-name, self-reported location, tweet content and language.

, in a global scenario, a combination of tweet content and tweet metadata can be used to achieve accurate country-level location classification of tweets, even when using a model trained on a dataset from a year prior to the classification of new tweets.

a combination of tweet content and metadata, such as the user’s self-declared location, real name and time zone, can lead to a significant improvement of the classification performance of tweets at the country-level, and that the use of tweet-intrinsic features can be leveraged to accurately classify new tweets, avoiding the need for retraining.
